subject: Biology
title: Evolutionary Mismatch and Modern Disease
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Evolutionary Mismatch and Modern Disease.

hook.text: Autoimmune diseases, allergies, and obesity barely existed in our ancestors. What changed?

buildup.text: Our immune systems evolved to fight constant parasitic infections. Modern hygiene removed the parasites.

discovery.text: Without parasites to fight, the immune system attacks harmless targets—pollen, food proteins, your own cells.

twist.text: Clinical trials show that deliberately introducing hookworms can reduce symptoms of Crohn's disease and allergies.

climax.text: The mismatch between our evolved biology and modern life drives many of today's chronic diseases.

punchline.text: We're too clean for our own immune systems.

quiz.question: What does the hygiene hypothesis suggest about modern allergies?
options: Lack of parasitic infections leaves the immune system overreactive
Modern allergens are more toxic than before
People now have weaker immune systems genetically

details.summary: Evolutionary mismatch occurs when traits that evolved for ancestral environments become maladaptive in modern ones. Our craving for sugar and fat evolved when calories were scarce but now drives obesity. Many modern diseases stem from this mismatch between our biology and lifestyle.
details.whyItMatters: Understanding mismatch explains the epidemic of obesity, diabetes, back pain, and anxiety in modern societies. Our bodies and minds were shaped for a world very different from the one we now inhabit, and this gap causes widespread suffering.
takeaways: Sugar and fat cravings evolved when these calories were rare and valuable
Our stress response is calibrated for acute physical threats, not chronic modern stress
Many allergies may result from immune systems understimulated by modern hygiene

faq.question: Why does our body crave unhealthy food?
faq.answer: These foods were not unhealthy in our ancestors' environment, where calories were scarce. Craving sugar and fat motivated efficient calorie seeking that aided survival. In our calorie-abundant modern environment, these once-adaptive cravings cause overconsumption.

faq.question: What does the hygiene hypothesis suggest about allergies?
faq.answer: Our immune systems evolved to combat parasites and pathogens encountered in ancient environments. Modern sanitation eliminated many of these. Without real threats to fight, the immune system may overreact to harmless substances like pollen and peanuts.
